preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(T, int) and T >= 1 and T <= 1000 for T in [int(stdin.split()[0])])
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 1000) representing the number of test cases.
Each test case consists of exactly three lines: N, Alice's stones (string A of length N), and Bob's stones (string B of length N).

preconditions.expression: all(len(A) == len(B) == N for N, A, B in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i*3+1]), stdin.splitlines()[i*3+2], stdin.splitlines()[i*3+3]) for i in range(T)])
preconditions.description: For each test case, N is the length of both Alice's and Bob's stone strings (1 ≤ N ≤ 10^5).

preconditions.expression: all(all(c.islower() for c in A) and all(c.islower() for c in B) for N, A, B in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i*3+1]), stdin.splitlines()[i*3+2], stdin.splitlines()[i*3+3]) for i in range(T)])
preconditions.description: All characters in Alice's and Bob's stones are lowercase English letters.

postconditions.expression: all(len(S) == 2 * N for N, A, B, S in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i*3+1]), stdin.splitlines()[i*3+2], stdin.splitlines()[i*3+3], stdout.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(T)])
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output string S has length exactly 2*N, where N is the number of stones each player has.

postconditions.expression: all(all(c in A + B for c in S) for N, A, B, S in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i*3+1]), stdin.splitlines()[i*3+2], stdin.splitlines()[i*3+3], stdout.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(T)])
postconditions.description: Every character in S is present in either Alice's or Bob's initial stones (A or B).

postconditions.expression: all(len(set(A) & set(S)) == len(A) and len(set(B) & set(S)) == len(B) for N, A, B, S in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i*3+1]), stdin.splitlines()[i*3+2], stdin.splitlines()[i*3+3], stdout.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(T)])
postconditions.description: All stones from Alice's and Bob's initial bags are used exactly once in S (no duplicates or omissions).

postconditions.expression: all(not any(S[i] < S[j] and i > j for i in range(2*N) for j in range(i)) for N, S in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i*3+1]), stdout.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(T)])
postconditions.description: The string S is the result of optimal play where Alice and Bob alternately place their stones to achieve lexicographically smallest and largest possible strings, respectively.
